pages.title: Restaurant Finance Services
pages.heading: Restaurant bookkeeping, payroll and financial review.
pages.description: Ready Margin handles restaurant bookkeeping, payroll preparation, bills and financial review. Choose the services you need and get a written scope and price.
pages.answer: Ready Margin handles restaurant bookkeeping, payroll preparation, bills and financial review. Choose the services you need and get a written scope and price.

sections.title: Choose the jobs you want us to handle
sections.body: You may need someone to reconcile the books every month, prepare payroll each cycle or investigate a cost problem. Tell us which jobs are falling behind and who handles them today. We recommend a service based on that work.
items: Supplier bills, cost review and CFO support

sections.title: Get the reports and the explanation
sections.body: For recurring work, we agree the inputs, reporting dates and review meetings. When a transaction is missing or a number changes, we ask for the supporting record and explain its effect on your accounts or cash.

sections.title: Know who approves what
sections.body: The proposal identifies the work we prepare, the decisions your restaurant approves and any tax or legal specialist involved. Your first demo is free; paid work starts under a separate agreement.

faqs.question: Can I choose only one service?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can quote for a defined job such as bookkeeping or payroll preparation. Additional work is agreed separately.

faqs.question: Does the service include software?
faqs.answer: The service uses a workspace to organize records and review tasks. Access and the tools used for your engagement are confirmed in your proposal.

pages.title: Restaurant Accounting Services
pages.heading: Monthly accounting for your restaurant.
pages.description: Monthly restaurant accounting with sales reconciliation, supplier costs, payroll records and financial reports. Review the results with Ready Margin.
pages.answer: Monthly restaurant accounting with sales reconciliation, supplier costs, payroll records and financial reports. Review the results with Ready Margin.

sections.title: Close the accounts for the same period
sections.body: We connect sales, card and delivery settlements, bank activity, supplier bills and payroll records to the month being reported. Missing invoices and unmatched amounts are identified before the reports are presented.

sections.title: Understand the changes in your P&L
sections.body: A higher cost can reflect a price change, a late bill or a different trading week. We review the relevant records and explain material movements. You receive the statements agreed in your scope and a list of items still awaiting confirmation.

sections.title: Separate monthly work from cleanup
sections.body: If the accounts are behind, we first establish the last reconciled period and the records available. Historic cleanup, tax returns and additional entities are quoted explicitly, so you know which work the monthly service covers.

related.label: Can one team handle restaurant payroll and bookkeeping?

faqs.question: How does accounting differ from bookkeeping?
faqs.answer: Bookkeeping records and reconciles transactions. Accounting adds period-end checks, financial statements and interpretation. The exact tasks are set out in your proposal.

faqs.question: Can Ready Margin work with my CPA?
faqs.answer: We can prepare the agreed accounts and supporting records for your CPA. The engagement names who handles tax advice, returns and any further accounting work.

pages.title: Restaurant Bookkeeping Services
pages.heading: Keep your restaurant’s books up to date.
pages.description: Restaurant bookkeeping for sales settlements, bank reconciliation, supplier invoices and payroll entries. Keep missing records from delaying the close.
pages.answer: Restaurant bookkeeping for sales settlements, bank reconciliation, supplier invoices and payroll entries. Keep missing records from delaying the close.

sections.title: Record the activity behind each trading day
sections.body: A POS sales report and a bank deposit often cover different dates and amounts. We organize settlement statements, fees, refunds and deposits so receipts can be traced to the underlying activity.

sections.title: Reconcile accounts and follow up on gaps
sections.body: We compare the ledger with bank and card records, check bill entries and obtain explanations for unmatched transactions. A missing receipt stays on the work list with the person who can supply it.

sections.title: Establish a repeatable collection routine
sections.body: We agree how records arrive and when questions are answered. You can add monthly accounting and reporting if you need them; backlog cleanup and tax preparation are separate items in the scope.

related.label: How to compare restaurant bookkeeping services

faqs.question: Can you take over books that are behind?
faqs.answer: We start by reviewing the last reconciled period, available statements and missing documents. Cleanup work and the start of ongoing bookkeeping are priced separately.

faqs.question: Does bookkeeping include taxes?
faqs.answer: Tax returns, payroll-tax processing and tax advice are included only when the agreement specifically names the responsible provider and work.

pages.title: Restaurant Payroll Services
pages.heading: Restaurant payroll preparation, checked before approval.
pages.description: Prepare restaurant payroll with reviewed hours, tip inputs and manager corrections. Ready Margin tracks outstanding questions before your approver signs off.
pages.answer: Prepare restaurant payroll with reviewed hours, tip inputs and manager corrections. Ready Margin tracks outstanding questions before your approver signs off.

sections.title: Check the pay-period inputs
sections.body: We compare recorded hours with schedules and manager-confirmed changes. Missing punches, rate questions and incomplete tip records are sent to the person who can resolve them before the agreed input cutoff.

sections.title: Keep corrections traceable
sections.body: The original entry, correction reason and manager confirmation belong together. We prepare the approved inputs for the payroll handoff and identify any question still waiting for an answer.

sections.title: Confirm the processor and approver
sections.body: Your engagement names the payroll processor, the restaurant’s authorized approver and the people responsible for tax tasks. Preparing records does not authorize a payroll run or establish that wages or taxes have been paid.

related.label: How to compare restaurant payroll services

resources.label: U.S. Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Division

faqs.question: Will Ready Margin approve our payroll?
faqs.answer: Your nominated approver retains payroll authorization. We prepare and review the inputs within the agreed service.

faqs.question: Do you replace our payroll provider?
faqs.answer: We review your existing provider first. Processing, direct connections and payroll-tax responsibilities are confirmed before service begins.

pages.title: Restaurant Tax and Compliance Support
pages.heading: Organize restaurant records for tax preparation.
pages.description: Prepare restaurant accounting and payroll records for tax review. Ready Margin coordinates document handoffs; filing and advice responsibilities are agreed separately.
pages.answer: Prepare restaurant accounting and payroll records for tax review. Ready Margin coordinates document handoffs; filing and advice responsibilities are agreed separately.

sections.title: Prepare the records your tax professional requests
sections.body: Closed accounts, payroll reports, settlement statements and supporting invoices may all be needed. We organize the documents in the agreed scope and identify missing records before the handoff.

sections.title: Assign each tax task to a responsible person
sections.body: Confirm who prepares the return, reviews it, authorizes payment and submits it. Use deadlines verified for your business by the responsible professional or authority. A document checklist cannot establish which taxes apply.

sections.title: Retain the submission evidence
sections.body: Where coordination is included, we follow up on outstanding documents and collect confirmation from the person completing the task. Tax advice, return preparation and filing are provided only under the relevant specialist engagement.

resources.label: IRS — Employer responsibilities when outsourcing payroll

faqs.question: Is Ready Margin a tax filing service?
faqs.answer: This page describes record preparation and coordination. Your proposal must separately name any provider responsible for returns, filings or tax advice.

faqs.question: Are taxes included in bookkeeping?
faqs.answer: They are separate responsibilities unless your written scope explicitly includes them. Confirm the provider and deliverables before work starts.

pages.title: Restaurant Compliance Workflow Support
pages.heading: Restaurant compliance tasks with assigned responsibilities.
pages.description: Coordinate restaurant compliance records, approvals and completion evidence. Confirm applicable requirements with the relevant authority or professional.
pages.answer: Coordinate restaurant compliance records, approvals and completion evidence. Confirm applicable requirements with the relevant authority or professional.

sections.title: Build the task list from confirmed requirements
sections.body: Start with the obligations that apply to your restaurant, location and activity. We help organize a list supplied or confirmed by the responsible adviser, including the documents and internal deadlines needed for each task.

sections.title: Separate preparation, approval and completion
sections.body: Name the person gathering records, the person authorizing the action and the person submitting or completing it. Each has a different responsibility. Keep unanswered questions visible before the deadline.

sections.title: Keep evidence of the completed action
sections.body: A reminder marked done does not prove a filing or payment happened. The handoff should retain the relevant receipt or confirmation. Legal interpretation, representation and certification require a separately appointed professional.

resources.label: U.S. Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Division

faqs.question: Can the service tell me every rule that applies?
faqs.answer: Applicable requirements must be confirmed by the relevant authority or adviser. Ready Margin can coordinate the agreed tasks and records.

faqs.question: Does outsourcing remove our responsibilities?
faqs.answer: No. The restaurant keeps its obligations and approvals. The agreement specifies which supporting tasks Ready Margin handles.

pages.title: Restaurant CFO Services
pages.heading: CFO support for restaurant cash and business decisions.
pages.description: Restaurant CFO support for cash planning, financial reporting and operating decisions. Review assumptions and options with the records behind them.
pages.answer: Restaurant CFO support for cash planning, financial reporting and operating decisions. Review assumptions and options with the records behind them.

sections.title: Start with the decision you need to make
sections.body: Hiring, an equipment purchase or a new location each needs a different analysis. We agree the question, deadline and available information before preparing the review.

sections.title: Build the cash and performance picture
sections.body: We review accounts, expected receipts, payroll and other commitments. Forecasts identify their assumptions and dates; incomplete information is marked so you can see how it affects the options.

sections.title: Evaluate options with your management team
sections.body: The review explains the effect of the scenarios we agree to examine and the records that need updating. You decide on spending, staffing and financing. Lending, investment, tax and legal advice are separate professional responsibilities.

related.label: When does a restaurant need a fractional CFO?

faqs.question: When is fractional CFO support useful?
faqs.answer: It can help when management needs regular cash planning, interpretation of results or analysis for a specific business decision. Reliable underlying accounts are a prerequisite.

faqs.question: Can you guarantee a better margin?
faqs.answer: No. We provide analysis and recommendations based on the agreed information. Outcomes depend on the restaurant’s decisions and trading conditions.

pages.title: Restaurant Financial Consulting
pages.heading: Get a financial review of a specific restaurant problem.
pages.description: Restaurant financial consulting for unexplained costs, cash pressure and planning questions. Get an assessment, supporting calculations and recommended actions.
pages.answer: Restaurant financial consulting for unexplained costs, cash pressure and planning questions. Get an assessment, supporting calculations and recommended actions.

sections.title: Define the question and the deliverable
sections.body: A consulting engagement might examine a supplier-cost increase, the economics of longer opening hours or cash required for a planned change. We agree the question, records and form of the final review before starting.

sections.title: Investigate the cause
sections.body: We compare periods and examine the relevant transactions and operating context. The assessment distinguishes confirmed findings from assumptions and explains what cannot yet be concluded.

sections.title: Turn the assessment into a work plan
sections.body: Recommendations identify what to change or check, who is responsible and how to review the result. You can commission follow-up work or recurring finance support separately.

faqs.question: How is consulting different from CFO support?
faqs.answer: Consulting can address a defined question or project. CFO support usually provides an ongoing financial review and planning relationship. Scope determines the distinction.

faqs.question: What should I bring to the first discussion?
faqs.answer: Describe the decision, deadline and systems you use. Detailed records can follow through an agreed sharing process.

pages.title: Restaurant Back-Office Services
pages.heading: Restaurant back-office support for the recurring finance jobs.
pages.description: Coordinate restaurant books, payroll inputs and supplier bills with Ready Margin. Agree the collection routine, review dates and approvals your team needs.
pages.answer: Coordinate restaurant books, payroll inputs and supplier bills with Ready Margin. Agree the collection routine, review dates and approvals your team needs.

sections.title: Assign the recurring finance tasks
sections.body: A manager may hold the attendance answer while a bookkeeper waits for a supplier invoice. We map those dependencies and identify which collection, preparation and follow-up tasks you want us to take on.

sections.title: Set a collection and review schedule
sections.body: Each recurring job needs its own inputs and cutoff. We organize agreed payroll, bookkeeping and bill tasks around those dates so managers know what to send and when.

sections.title: Keep operating authority with the restaurant
sections.body: Your team confirms deliveries, worked hours and other operating facts, then gives the defined approvals. We prepare the finance records and maintain the work list. General administration and specialist tasks are included only where named.

faqs.question: Does back-office support cover all administration?
faqs.answer: No. The written scope lists the finance and coordination tasks included. HR, legal, tax and other specialist services require explicit arrangements.

faqs.question: Can you work with existing staff?
faqs.answer: Yes. We agree how Ready Margin, your managers and existing advisers divide preparation, review and approval.

pages.title: Restaurant Accounts Payable Services
pages.heading: Know which supplier bills need review and payment approval.
pages.description: Restaurant accounts payable support for invoices, credits, due dates and approval status. Ready Margin prepares the bill records for your payment decisions.
pages.answer: Restaurant accounts payable support for invoices, credits, due dates and approval status. Ready Margin prepares the bill records for your payment decisions.

sections.title: Organize invoices and credits by supplier
sections.body: We maintain the agreed bill records, including invoice references, amounts and due dates. Where documents are available, we compare the invoice with the order or delivery and flag duplicates or unexplained differences.

sections.title: Resolve the question before approval
sections.body: A missing credit, changed pack size or disputed delivery should be identified in the bill review. We send the question to the supplier or restaurant contact and keep the response with the invoice.

sections.title: Review obligations alongside cash
sections.body: The approved and outstanding bill lists support your payment planning. Your authorized person decides on payment. We record the supplied payment evidence; a reviewed invoice is not evidence that a transfer was made.

related.label: Is Ready Margin software or a managed service?

faqs.question: Do you pay suppliers on our behalf?
faqs.answer: Payment execution is included only if specifically agreed. The restaurant retains the defined approval authority.

faqs.question: Can disputed bills stay separate from approved bills?
faqs.answer: Yes. Review status and the outstanding question should be retained with each invoice so it is not mistaken for an approved payment.

pages.title: Restaurant Cash Flow Management
pages.heading: Plan restaurant cash around receipts and payment dates.
pages.description: Review restaurant bank balances, settlement timing, payroll and supplier obligations. Build a dated cash plan with explicit assumptions and unresolved items.
pages.answer: Review restaurant bank balances, settlement timing, payroll and supplier obligations. Build a dated cash plan with explicit assumptions and unresolved items.

sections.title: Establish today’s position
sections.body: Date the account balances and confirm which accounts are included. Reconcile receipts already received, then list payroll, supplier bills, rent and other known obligations through the period you need to plan.

sections.title: Check when the money arrives
sections.body: Sales and receipts happen on different dates. Card settlements, delivery payouts, refunds and fees can change the cash available before a payment. We check the supporting statements and identify estimates.

sections.title: Review the plan before committing money
sections.body: A cash review sets out timing assumptions, incomplete inputs and the decisions due before the next update. We can model agreed scenarios where the records support them; projections do not guarantee future balances.

related.label: How should a restaurant cash-flow review start?

faqs.question: Why can a busy restaurant be short of cash?
faqs.answer: Sales may settle later, while payroll and supplier bills fall due now. Existing commitments and refunds also affect the balance available to spend.

faqs.question: Is the demo cash screen a live forecast?
faqs.answer: No. The public demo uses sample records and identifies missing projection inputs. Your service review depends on the records and scope agreed for your business.

pages.title: Restaurant Food Cost Management
pages.heading: Find what is driving your restaurant’s food cost.
pages.description: Review supplier prices, recipes, portions, stock counts and sales mix. Ready Margin helps identify the source of a food-cost change before you act.
pages.answer: Review supplier prices, recipes, portions, stock counts and sales mix. Ready Margin helps identify the source of a food-cost change before you act.

sections.title: Separate price changes from usage changes
sections.body: Compare like-for-like items and units before concluding that a supplier raised prices. Then examine purchases, counts and sales for a common period to establish whether the movement is in price, usage or timing.

sections.title: Check the kitchen’s working assumptions
sections.body: Recipes, usable yield, portion sizes and waste records affect the calculation. We review the agreed records with purchasing and kitchen contacts, identifying estimates and gaps that could change the result.

sections.title: Agree a specific change to review
sections.body: The finding may lead to a supplier query, a portion check or an update to recipe costs. Management decides on menu and purchasing changes. We agree which measures will be reviewed afterward; a fixed savings result is not promised.

related.label: How can a restaurant investigate high food cost?

faqs.question: Can invoice totals tell us why food cost rose?
faqs.answer: An invoice is one input. Pack size, quantity, inventory timing, waste and sales mix may also explain the change.

faqs.question: Do you run our inventory system?
faqs.answer: Inventory recording or system administration is included only if named in the scope. We first assess the records and tools you already use.

pages.title: Restaurant Labor Cost Management
pages.heading: Understand labor cost from the schedule through payroll.
pages.description: Compare restaurant schedules, attendance, wage inputs and sales for the same period. Investigate labor-cost changes with the managers who know the shifts.
pages.answer: Compare restaurant schedules, attendance, wage inputs and sales for the same period. Investigate labor-cost changes with the managers who know the shifts.

sections.title: Compare planned and recorded hours
sections.body: The schedule shows intended coverage. Attendance records show the hours recorded after service. We compare both with manager-confirmed changes, rather than treating a difference as an error without checking.

sections.title: Use a consistent employment-cost basis
sections.body: Agree which wage costs, payroll taxes, benefits and other employment costs belong in the analysis. A base-wage estimate from a schedule is not the full cost of labor. Align the cost and sales periods before comparing percentages.

sections.title: Review staffing options in operating context
sections.body: Opening hours, sales mix and service requirements matter to coverage. We explain the financial comparison and outstanding records; management decides on staffing and pay, with appropriate employment advice where required.

related.label: How can a restaurant review labor cost?

resources.label: U.S. Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Division

faqs.question: Can we use scheduled wages as actual labor cost?
faqs.answer: Scheduled base wages are a planning input. Worked hours, corrections and other employment costs must be considered for the actual-cost review.

faqs.question: Does lower labor cost always mean better performance?
faqs.answer: No. Coverage, service quality and trading conditions need to be considered alongside the financial result.

pages.title: Restaurant Tip Management Support
pages.heading: Trace restaurant tip inputs before payroll approval.
pages.description: Organize restaurant check records, tip inputs, allocation rules and corrections. Resolve missing evidence with the responsible manager before the payroll handoff.
pages.answer: Organize restaurant check records, tip inputs, allocation rules and corrections. Resolve missing evidence with the responsible manager before the payroll handoff.

sections.title: Identify the source and period
sections.body: We review the agreed check and tip records for the pay period, including unmatched employee names, incomplete assignments and held amounts. Each exception needs the underlying record and a person who can confirm it.

sections.title: Apply the restaurant’s confirmed rules
sections.body: Your restaurant supplies and authorizes the applicable tip policy and allocation rules. Where a rule cannot be established or a record cannot be matched, the question is escalated rather than resolved by an assumption.

sections.title: Document adjustments and the approval
sections.body: Corrections retain the source amount, reason and authorizing person. We prepare the agreed tip inputs for payroll review. Employment-law interpretation and resolution of legal disputes belong with the appropriate professional.

resources.label: U.S. Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Division

faqs.question: Can Ready Margin write our tip policy?
faqs.answer: Policy and legal advice require an explicitly appointed professional. Our record-preparation work uses rules confirmed and approved by your restaurant.

faqs.question: What happens to an unmatched tip record?
faqs.answer: It stays identified as unresolved while the responsible person supplies the missing employee assignment or other evidence.

pages.title: Restaurant Inventory and Cost Control
pages.heading: Make restaurant inventory counts useful for cost review.
pages.description: Connect restaurant stock counts, purchases, recipes and transfers to the reporting period. Investigate cost differences with comparable quantities and units.
pages.answer: Connect restaurant stock counts, purchases, recipes and transfers to the reporting period. Investigate cost differences with comparable quantities and units.

sections.title: Agree how and when stock is counted
sections.body: Use consistent units, categories and count dates. Record the person confirming the count and any items estimated or omitted. Counts from different dates can distort a cost comparison.

sections.title: Connect the movements between counts
sections.body: Opening stock, purchases, transfers and closing stock help explain consumption. Credits, waste and recipe assumptions add context. We organize the agreed records and ask the kitchen or purchasing contact about gaps.

sections.title: Investigate the variance before changing orders
sections.body: A variance can reflect a counting error, unit conversion, timing or actual usage. We document the likely explanation and further checks, then management decides on purchasing or kitchen changes.

related.label: Restaurant recipe costing: units, yield and portions

faqs.question: Does this include physical stock counts?
faqs.answer: Physical counting is included only if explicitly agreed. We otherwise use records confirmed by your restaurant and identify their limitations.

faqs.question: Can you review different supplier pack sizes?
faqs.answer: Yes, where the necessary item and unit information is available. Comparable units are needed before a price or usage comparison is meaningful.

pages.title: Restaurant Turnaround Consulting
pages.heading: Restaurant turnaround support starts with the cash and deadlines.
pages.description: Assess restaurant cash pressure, overdue work and urgent operating decisions. Ready Margin helps prioritize the finance review and assign follow-up actions.
pages.eyebrow: Restaurant turnaround / Financial and operating support
pages.answer: Assess restaurant cash pressure, overdue work and urgent operating decisions. Ready Margin helps prioritize the finance review and assign follow-up actions.

sections.title: Identify the decisions that cannot wait
sections.body: Start with current balances, payments due and the immediate management deadline. We distinguish confirmed obligations from disputed or estimated amounts and establish what information is missing.

sections.title: Review the sources of pressure
sections.body: Late accounts, higher costs and settlement delays call for different work. We examine the available records, agree the order of investigation and explain the limits of the assessment.

sections.title: Build a dated action list
sections.body: Each action has a responsible person, required input and review date. We update the plan as facts change. Turnaround support does not guarantee recovery; financing, legal and insolvency decisions need the relevant advisers.

faqs.question: Can you start before the accounts are current?
faqs.answer: We can discuss immediate priorities using the information available, then identify the accounting work needed to support a fuller review.

faqs.question: Is turnaround support a financing service?
faqs.answer: No. Any borrowing, restructuring or insolvency work requires the appropriate separately engaged adviser or provider.

pages.title: Restaurant Profitability Consulting
pages.heading: Review your restaurant’s profit and cost drivers.
pages.description: Review restaurant sales mix, food cost, labor and overhead to investigate weak profitability. Get a financial explanation and options to discuss with management.
pages.answer: Review restaurant sales mix, food cost, labor and overhead to investigate weak profitability. Get a financial explanation and options to discuss with management.

sections.title: Establish the result you are reviewing
sections.body: Confirm the period, accounts included and whether costs are complete. A profit comparison needs consistent treatment of payroll, supplier bills, stock and overhead before it can support a decision.

sections.title: Examine the drivers separately
sections.body: A change in sales mix, ingredient usage, staffing or fixed costs can reduce margin in different ways. We investigate the agreed areas with transaction evidence and context from the restaurant.

sections.title: Evaluate changes before implementing them
sections.body: We explain the assumptions behind pricing, purchasing or operating scenarios and the information still needed. Your management team chooses the response and a date to review the effect. Results are not guaranteed.

faqs.question: Will more sales fix low profitability?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The contribution from those sales, their costs and the restaurant’s overhead determine their effect on profit.

faqs.question: How does this differ from a food-cost review?
faqs.answer: A profitability review considers the wider result, including sales mix, labor and overhead. A food-cost engagement focuses on the agreed food and purchasing records.

pages.title: Multi-Location Restaurant Finance
pages.heading: Financial reporting for restaurant groups.
pages.description: Coordinate accounting, payroll inputs and financial reporting across restaurant locations. Use consistent reporting definitions with local exceptions identified.
pages.answer: Coordinate accounting, payroll inputs and financial reporting across restaurant locations. Use consistent reporting definitions with local exceptions identified.

sections.title: Agree the group reporting structure
sections.body: Define the entities, locations, accounts and periods before combining results. Shared costs and transfers need consistent treatment so the group total and location views can be understood.

sections.title: Keep local questions with local contacts
sections.body: A late invoice or missing attendance correction at one site can distort the comparison. We identify incomplete inputs and route questions to the manager who can confirm the facts.

sections.title: Review differences with operating context
sections.body: Opening hours, format and recent changes can explain location performance. The review shows the agreed group and site measures, their reporting basis and actions for each responsible person.

faqs.question: Can all locations use one reporting timetable?
faqs.answer: We can agree a common timetable while identifying differences in source systems, payroll periods or data availability.

faqs.question: Can you report on separate legal entities?
faqs.answer: Entity coverage, intercompany treatment and specialist accounting requirements must be specified in the engagement.

pages.title: Outsourced Restaurant Finance Team
pages.heading: An outsourced finance team for your restaurant.
pages.description: An outsourced restaurant finance team for bookkeeping, payroll preparation and financial review. Define the responsibilities alongside your managers and advisers.
pages.answer: An outsourced restaurant finance team for bookkeeping, payroll preparation and financial review. Define the responsibilities alongside your managers and advisers.

sections.title: Decide what stays in-house
sections.body: Your managers know the shifts, deliveries and operating changes. We map those responsibilities alongside the finance jobs you want to outsource, including any existing bookkeeper, accountant or payroll provider.

sections.title: Name the person responsible for each service
sections.body: The agreement specifies the preparation, checks, reporting dates and follow-up Ready Margin handles. Your team has a defined route for submitting inputs and answering questions.

sections.title: Confirm your approval responsibilities
sections.body: The restaurant retains the named payroll, payment and operating approvals. Extra locations, cleanup or specialist work are agreed as scope changes. We quote after understanding the workload in your free demo.

faqs.question: Is this a replacement for every finance role?
faqs.answer: No. We agree the jobs to outsource and how they connect with your existing team and specialist advisers.

faqs.question: How much does an outsourced finance team cost?
faqs.answer: Pricing depends on locations, transaction and payroll workload, current records and the support selected. We provide the scope and fees in writing.
